payload.claim: `_restore_source` (and the `source_reverted` context manager wrapping it) only checks the exit code of `git checkout HEAD -- paths`, never that the tree is actually clean afterward, even though the acceptance criteria and this module's own docstring promise 'the worktree the other gates measure is the worktree they started with' and that a tree `source_reverted` 'cannot restore is an error rather than a quietly dirty tree the committed gate blames on the task.' `run_tests(subset)` runs a real test process inside the same worktree while the source is reverted, and any artifact it leaves outside the exact `paths` list (a stray file, a build/log artifact not covered by `.gitignore`) is invisible to the checkout-return-code check, survives into the `committed_gate(worktree.dirty_paths(container))` call that immediately follows, and would fail the task's `committed` gate for dirt this gate itself produced during REPAIR — the exact mis-blamed-diff scenario the docstring says must become `error` instead. None of the tests added in this diff exercise real git/filesystem behavior (all use fakes for `reverted`/`run_tests`), so this gap between the documented guarantee and the actual implementation is invisible to the suite.
